question: What methods reduce hallucination in RAG systems?

key_papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

findings.text: Trains one LM to retrieve on demand and to critique retrieved passages and its own output using special reflection tokens.

key_papers.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation

findings.text: A lightweight retrieval evaluator scores retrieved documents and triggers corrective actions such as web search when retrieval is unreliable.

key_papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

findings.text: Combining a parametric generator with non-parametric retrieval memory gives more factual, specific generations than a parametric-only model.

key_papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey

findings.text: Organises RAG research into Naive RAG, Advanced RAG and Modular RAG paradigms.

question: How do dense retrieval methods compare to sparse methods for open-domain question answering?

key_papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

findings.text: A dual-encoder dense retriever beats BM25 by a large margin in top-20 passage retrieval accuracy on open-domain QA.

key_papers.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval

findings.text: Constructing hard negatives from an asynchronously refreshed approximate nearest neighbour index improves dense retriever training.

key_papers.title: BEIR: A Heterogenous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models

findings.text: BM25 remains a robust zero-shot baseline across heterogeneous datasets, while dense retrievers generalise poorly out of domain.

key_papers.title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning

findings.text: Unsupervised contrastive pre-training yields dense retrievers that are competitive with BM25.

question: What prompting techniques improve the reasoning ability of large language models?

key_papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

findings.text: Prompting with intermediate reasoning steps (chain of thought) substantially improves arithmetic and commonsense reasoning in sufficiently large models.

key_papers.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models

findings.text: Sampling diverse reasoning paths and taking the most consistent answer improves over greedy chain-of-thought decoding.

key_papers.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners

findings.text: Appending 'Let's think step by step' elicits multi-step reasoning without any few-shot examples.

key_papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

findings.text: Searching over a tree of intermediate thoughts with lookahead and backtracking solves tasks such as Game of 24 far better than chain of thought.

question: How can large language models be fine-tuned efficiently with limited compute?

key_papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

findings.text: Freezing the pre-trained weights and training low-rank update matrices cuts trainable parameters by orders of magnitude with little quality loss.

key_papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

findings.text: Backpropagating through a frozen 4-bit quantised model into LoRA adapters (NormalFloat data type) allows fine-tuning a 65B model on a single GPU.

key_papers.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation

findings.text: Optimising a small continuous prefix while keeping the language model frozen is a lightweight alternative to full fine-tuning.

key_papers.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning

findings.text: Learning soft prompts with a frozen model closes the gap to full fine-tuning as model size grows.

question: What are the main approaches to evaluating the factuality of language model generations?

key_papers.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation

findings.text: Breaks a generation into atomic facts and reports the share supported by a knowledge source.

key_papers.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models

findings.text: Detects hallucinations without external resources by checking consistency across multiple sampled responses.

key_papers.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods

findings.text: A benchmark of questions that elicit imitative falsehoods shows larger models can be less truthful.

key_papers.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation

findings.text: Distinguishes intrinsic from extrinsic hallucination and surveys metrics and mitigation methods.
